summary: Zara rigs a prime-number bioluminescent pulse sequence to blind Isla, but accidentally dazzles Willow instead.
science_vegetable: Enzymatic luciferin-luciferase oxidation gated by voltage-sensitive ion channels flashing in prime-number sequences and optical polarization modulation.
narrative_prose:
The cave didn't end; it drowned.

Zara stood at the edge of the subterranean lake. The water was black, motionless, and heavy with iron, the smell of damp ozone and copper hanging thick in the air. She could almost taste the metallic tang on her tongue.

She waded in. Her suit adjusted, pressurizing against the tactile weight of the deep. The enzymatic luciferin-luciferase oxidation gated by voltage-sensitive ion channels flashed in prime-number sequences and optical polarization modulation. She'd spent all morning coaxing the abyssal chemosynthetic cephalopod into a 3-5-7-11 strobe to attract it closer. It was a precise, photophore syntax designed for one thing: temporarily overloading Isla's optic filters while she was mapping the feed pens, unable to defend against the sudden glare.

But Isla stepped aside to tighten a chronosphere relay bracket.

The strobe hit Willow instead, whose optic nerves seemed to consume the light completely. The alchemist dropped a vial of stabilizing epoxy as the sudden blue light shattered her vision.

Zara froze. Her Gemini override snapped. The silence vanished. "If you're complaining and no one is laughing, you're complaining wrong," Zara babbled, moving at breakneck speed. "The polarity was set to 45 degrees, which should have deflected off Isla's secondary visor, but instead the prime-number burst refracted right into your retinas and I am so, so sorry, the logic gates in the calcium-ions must be completely blown and now I have to muck out the Sanctuary feed pens every morning as penance while you are temporarily blinded by my terrible spatial awareness!"

Willow groaned, rubbing her temples. "Zara, breathe."
